{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Import the Prisma client before updating Salesforce credentials",
      "body": "The new database update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor defines it. This fails type checking and, if checks are skipped, fails at runtime before getClient returns a Salesforce connection. Salesforce event creation, updates, and deletion are therefore broken even when credential sharing is disabled."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Persist parsed token data rather than the safe-parse result",
      "body": "parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safe-parse result shaped as `{ success: true, data: tokens }`, whereas the previous schema.parse call returned the tokens themselves. Passing this result directly as the credential key stores the wrapper instead of the Google credential fields. The next service initialization fails googleCredentialSchema.parse because access_token and the other fields are nested under data. This corrupts credentials on ordinary Google refreshes even with sharing disabled."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Preserve the response contract expected by each refresh caller",
      "body": "The sharing branch always returns a native Fetch Response, but several callbacks normally return different objects. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read `.data`, while HubSpot reads SDK fields such as `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn` directly. None of these callers deserializes the shared Fetch Response, so sharing produces undefined token fields or throws before refreshing credentials. Parse and adapt the shared response, or update these callers to consume a consistent response contract."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Use actual response fields in the minimum token schema",
      "body": "Calling toString() on these Zod schemas produces the literal property name `[object Object]`; it does not match arbitrary response properties. Both computed keys use that name, so the optional unknown property also overwrites the numeric requirement. Since z.object strips unknown properties, a shared response loses expires_in, expiry_date, and any supplied refresh_token. For example, Zoom subsequently computes its expiry from undefined, while Office365 receives no updated expiry."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 26,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not replace omitted refresh tokens with a literal placeholder",
      "body": "This fallback also runs when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller previously merged the response into the stored credentials to retain the existing token. Adding the literal `refresh_token` now overwrites that valid stored token, causing the next direct OAuth refresh to fail. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Send the credential owner's user ID rather than the credential ID",
      "body": "The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is sent to the parent platform as calcomUserId, but this call supplies the Credential table's primary key. Credential IDs and user IDs are unrelated. Whenever this ID matches another user, the parent is asked to refresh and return that other user's Bigin integration; otherwise the lookup fails. Propagate credential.userId through this refresh path instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Use the actual Zoom app slug in delegated refresh requests",
      "body": "The delegated request sends appSlug `zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and `zoom` is the app-store slug. A parent platform using the same slug contract as the credential webhook cannot find this integration under `zoomvideo`, so Zoom refreshes fail whenever sharing is enabled."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Delegate Salesforce refreshes to the configured sync endpoint",
      "body": "This new refresh request always goes directly to Salesforce and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, even when credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured. Applying the sharing-aware parser afterward does not delegate the refresh. Synced credentials without a local provider refresh token fail here, while credentials containing one are refreshed outside the parent platform rather than through the configured source of truth."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Keep local refresh-token expiry checks out of delegated refreshes",
      "body": "The new delegation is reached only after refreshAccessToken checks the locally stored refresh token and deletes the credential if that token is missing or expired. In sharing mode, the parent owns refreshes and the helper specifies that its response only needs an access token and expiry; the local refresh token can therefore be absent or stale while the parent can still supply a valid access token. This path deletes the synced integration instead of contacting the parent. Perform the provider-only validation inside the direct OAuth fallback."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Accept the token-only sync response in the Webex refresh path",
      "body": "After delegating to the sync endpoint, this adapter still validates the response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. The documented shared response containing only the access token and expiry is rejected as an invalid refresh response. The sharing path needs to consume that response and retain the necessary existing credential metadata rather than require a complete Webex OAuth response."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 61,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Preserve absolute expiry dates returned by the sync endpoint",
      "body": "A shared response containing access_token and a future expiry_date reaches code that unconditionally replaces expiry_date with Date.now() plus expires_in, defaulting the missing expires_in to zero. The freshly obtained token is consequently stored as immediately expired, forcing another delegated refresh on every subsequent operation. Handle the shared absolute expiry separately from Microsoft's expires_in duration."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 78,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Clear the invalid flag when replacing credentials",
      "body": "Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials invalid after unrecoverable authentication failures. This webhook finds those same records but updates only their key, leaving invalid=true after valid replacement tokens are synchronized. The webhook reports success without restoring the installation's validity. Reset the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 83,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Make credential creation idempotent under concurrent webhooks",
      "body": "The findFirst followed by create is not atomic. Two concurrent deliveries for a user's first credential can both observe no record and create separate credentials for the same user and app. Later webhook deliveries update only one arbitrary match, leaving the other credential stale and the database inconsistent with the parent source of truth. Serialize the per-user/app operation or enforce an appropriate idempotency constraint."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Import the Prisma client before updating Salesforce credentials
findings.body: The new database update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor defines it. This fails type checking and, if checks are skipped, fails at runtime before getClient returns a Salesforce connection. Salesforce event creation, updates, and deletion are therefore broken even when credential sharing is disabled.

findings.title: Persist parsed token data rather than the safe-parse result
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safe-parse result shaped as `{ success: true, data: tokens }`, whereas the previous schema.parse call returned the tokens themselves. Passing this result directly as the credential key stores the wrapper instead of the Google credential fields. The next service initialization fails googleCredentialSchema.parse because access_token and the other fields are nested under data. This corrupts credentials on ordinary Google refreshes even with sharing disabled.

findings.title: Preserve the response contract expected by each refresh caller
findings.body: The sharing branch always returns a native Fetch Response, but several callbacks normally return different objects. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read `.data`, while HubSpot reads SDK fields such as `.accessToken` and `.expiresIn` directly. None of these callers deserializes the shared Fetch Response, so sharing produces undefined token fields or throws before refreshing credentials. Parse and adapt the shared response, or update these callers to consume a consistent response contract.

findings.title: Use actual response fields in the minimum token schema
findings.body: Calling toString() on these Zod schemas produces the literal property name `[object Object]`; it does not match arbitrary response properties. Both computed keys use that name, so the optional unknown property also overwrites the numeric requirement. Since z.object strips unknown properties, a shared response loses expires_in, expiry_date, and any supplied refresh_token. For example, Zoom subsequently computes its expiry from undefined, while Office365 receives no updated expiry.

findings.title: Do not replace omitted refresh tokens with a literal placeholder
findings.body: This fallback also runs when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller previously merged the response into the stored credentials to retain the existing token. Adding the literal `refresh_token` now overwrites that valid stored token, causing the next direct OAuth refresh to fail. Preserve the existing token when the provider does not return a replacement.

findings.body: The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is sent to the parent platform as calcomUserId, but this call supplies the Credential table's primary key. Credential IDs and user IDs are unrelated. Whenever this ID matches another user, the parent is asked to refresh and return that other user's Bigin integration; otherwise the lookup fails. Propagate credential.userId through this refresh path instead.

findings.title: Use the actual Zoom app slug in delegated refresh requests
findings.body: The delegated request sends appSlug `zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and `zoom` is the app-store slug. A parent platform using the same slug contract as the credential webhook cannot find this integration under `zoomvideo`, so Zoom refreshes fail whenever sharing is enabled.

findings.title: Delegate Salesforce refreshes to the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: This new refresh request always goes directly to Salesforce and never calls refreshOAuthTokens, even when credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured. Applying the sharing-aware parser afterward does not delegate the refresh. Synced credentials without a local provider refresh token fail here, while credentials containing one are refreshed outside the parent platform rather than through the configured source of truth.

findings.title: Keep local refresh-token expiry checks out of delegated refreshes
findings.body: The new delegation is reached only after refreshAccessToken checks the locally stored refresh token and deletes the credential if that token is missing or expired. In sharing mode, the parent owns refreshes and the helper specifies that its response only needs an access token and expiry; the local refresh token can therefore be absent or stale while the parent can still supply a valid access token. This path deletes the synced integration instead of contacting the parent. Perform the provider-only validation inside the direct OAuth fallback.

findings.title: Accept the token-only sync response in the Webex refresh path
findings.body: After delegating to the sync endpoint, this adapter still validates the response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. The documented shared response containing only the access token and expiry is rejected as an invalid refresh response. The sharing path needs to consume that response and retain the necessary existing credential metadata rather than require a complete Webex OAuth response.

findings.title: Preserve absolute expiry dates returned by the sync endpoint
findings.body: A shared response containing access_token and a future expiry_date reaches code that unconditionally replaces expiry_date with Date.now() plus expires_in, defaulting the missing expires_in to zero. The freshly obtained token is consequently stored as immediately expired, forcing another delegated refresh on every subsequent operation. Handle the shared absolute expiry separately from Microsoft's expires_in duration.

findings.title: Clear the invalid flag when replacing credentials
findings.body: Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials invalid after unrecoverable authentication failures. This webhook finds those same records but updates only their key, leaving invalid=true after valid replacement tokens are synchronized. The webhook reports success without restoring the installation's validity. Reset the invalid flag when accepting replacement credentials.

findings.title: Make credential creation idempotent under concurrent webhooks
findings.body: The findFirst followed by create is not atomic. Two concurrent deliveries for a user's first credential can both observe no record and create separate credentials for the same user and app. Later webhook deliveries update only one arbitrary match, leaving the other credential stale and the database inconsistent with the parent source of truth. Serialize the per-user/app operation or enforce an appropriate idempotency constraint.
